record.paper_title: Twenty open problems in quantum control
record.context_brief: Measurement restrictions and geodesic entropy extraction
record.original_question: For feedback protocols implemented through irreversible coupling, can one quantitatively characterize how much performance is lost when the controller is restricted to measurement followed by conditional feedback, and can that loss be related to geodesic evolutions in the joint system-auxiliary Hilbert space that extract entropy as quickly as possible?

evidence.quote: What is shown in [6] is that, under a bound on the Hamiltonian that performs the interaction between the system and auxiliary (an interaction that is also required to make a measure), the fastest way to extract all the entropy from the system using CFC is to follow a geodesic in the joint Hilbert space of the system and auxiliary [6].
Problem 4: Is it possible to show quantitatively how the restriction to measurement and feedback limits the performance of feedback via irreversible coupling, and how this relates to geodesics?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a quantum system $S$ coupled to an auxiliary quantum system $A$, both modeled on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_S$ and $\mathcal{H}_A$, with joint Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_S \otimes \mathcal{H}_A$. Two cooling/feedback paradigms are compared:

(i) Coherent Feedback Control (CFC): a unitary interaction $U(t) = \exp(-i H t)$ generated by a Hamiltonian $H$ on $\mathcal{H}_S \otimes \mathcal{H}_A$, with a fixed bound $\|H\| \le E$ on its operator norm, that transfers entropy from $S$ to $A$. Under such a norm bound, the quickest possible extraction of all entropy from $S$ into $A$ is achieved when the joint pure state of $S\otimes A$ evolves along a geodesic of the Fubini–Study metric on the projective Hilbert space $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{H}_S \otimes \mathcal{H}_A)$.

(ii) Measurement-and-Feedback Control (MFC): the controller is restricted to (a) performing a (possibly generalized) measurement on $A$ after a system–auxiliary interaction, and (b) applying a unitary on $S$ conditioned on the classical outcome.

For an arbitrary initial state $\rho_S$ of the system (with the auxiliary prepared in a fixed pure reference state) and a fixed Hamiltonian energy budget $\|H\|\le E$ for any system–auxiliary coupling used, define the cooling time $T_{\mathrm{CFC}}(\rho_S, E, \varepsilon)$ (resp. $T_{\mathrm{MFC}}(\rho_S, E, \varepsilon)$) as the infimum over admissible CFC (resp. MFC) protocols of the time required to bring $S$ to a state with von Neumann entropy at most $\varepsilon$.

Problem. Provide a quantitative characterization of the gap
$$\Delta(\rho_S, E, \varepsilon) \;=\; T_{\mathrm{MFC}}(\rho_S, E, \varepsilon) \;-\; T_{\mathrm{CFC}}(\rho_S, E, \varepsilon),$$
i.e. the performance loss incurred by restricting the controller from coherent feedback through irreversible coupling to measurement-plus-conditional-feedback. In particular, derive sharp lower (and, if possible, matching upper) bounds on $\Delta$ expressed in terms of geometric data of the joint Hilbert space — for example, the Fubini–Study length of the optimal CFC geodesic that extracts entropy from $S$ and a quantitative measure of how far MFC trajectories must deviate from such geodesics — and characterize the protocols (if any) for which the bound is saturated.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches for a quantitative comparison between measurement-based feedback and coherent (irreversible-coupling) feedback in terms of geodesic entropy extraction in the joint system–auxiliary Hilbert space did not turn up a definitive resolution. Related literature on measurement-based quantum thermal machines and quantum feedback control discusses performance trade-offs but does not appear to provide a sharp geometric characterization of the loss as posed. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Quantum feedback: Theory, experiments, and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive review of quantum feedback covering measurement-based and coherent feedback paradigms.
status_evidence.claim: The review surveys quantum feedback paradigms but does not provide a sharp geometric (geodesic-based) characterization of the performance loss between measurement feedback and coherent feedback under a Hamiltonian norm bound.

status_evidence.title: Measurement-Based Quantum Thermal Machines with Feedback Control
status_evidence.snippet: Studies coupled-qubit thermal machines driven by measurement and feedback, comparing performance of measurement-based protocols.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on measurement-based feedback thermodynamics does not address the specific geodesic-gap quantification posed.
